solutions.check: 30 entries, 60 crossings, 0 conflicts; answers matched to the grid by number, direction and length

clue.text: Press button — it fails to open quick application

indicators.note: the word for pressing a button loses its opening letter, so it no longer starts properly

parts.note: to press a mouse button is to click

explanation.surface: Someone jabs a button but the program they want won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it fails to open' removes C, the first letter of CLICK. 'application' is not software but a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick coat of paint or polish is called a lick, as in 'a lick of paint'.

clue.text: Part of country road in which bank employee loses energy

indicators.note: in which says the road holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the bank worker

parts.note: a cashier works at a bank counter
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A rural road where a bank teller runs out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes E out of CASHIER to give CASHIR, which goes 'in' LANE. LANCASHIRE is an English county in the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: This English county in the north-west is a region of the country of England.

clue.text: A book set in part of America — that's intriguing

definitions.note: the clue describes a group that plots; the answer is that group itself

indicators.note: set in means placed inside

parts.note: Cal is short for California

explanation.surface: A novel with an American setting that sounds gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in' puts A and B inside CAL (California). 'intriguing' means plotting, not fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret faction scheming for power is a group of plotters, people engaged in intrigue.

clue.text: Legal phraseology that doesn't give you the big picture

definitions.text: Legal phraseology that doesn't give you the big picture

parts.words: Legal phraseology that doesn't give you the big picture
parts.note: the fine conditions in a contract are printed tiny, so literally they are no big picture, and they also hide the overall meaning

explanation.surface: A complaint about contract terms that obscure the overall deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big picture' works twice: the type is literally tiny, and the terms hide what you are really agreeing to.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract terms in tiny type are the classic legal wording that readers miss.

clue.text: Dreadful porno mag, husband's paper

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly made, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A spouse's awful smutty magazine is found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges PORNOMAG into MONOGRAP; H follows. 'paper' is an academic essay, not a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarly treatise on one subject is a learned paper or essay.

clue.text: A slow mover, one put into the ground not having died

indicators.note: put into means placed inside the other piece
not having means a letter is removed from the ground's name

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sluggish person is buried before they have even died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' takes D out of LORDS (Lord's, the London cricket ground) to give LORS; 'put into' places I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This small primate of South and South-East Asia is famous for creeping along branches very sluggishly.

clue.text: Son wearing good clothes is a complete mess

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

indicators.note: wearing means having clothes around one, so the son sits inside the clothes

parts.note: gear is informal for clothes

explanation.surface: A boy dressed in his best yet looking a total shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts the son in the clothes. To 'make a pig's ear of' something is a British idiom for botching it.
explanation.definitionFit: This British idiom names a bungled job, a thoroughly messed-up piece of work.

clue.text: Narrow-minded, about to become a conductor? No

indicators.note: about means going around, so the parochial word surrounds the next one

parts.note: insular means parochial and narrow-minded

explanation.surface: A bigot is set to take up the baton in front of an orchestra, and refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the narrow-minded word round 'to'. 'conductor' suggests an orchestra; here it is electrical, and 'No' turns it into its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A material that blocks heat or electricity is the opposite of something that carries current.

clue.text: Move briskly to dismiss fourth member of quintet

indicators.note: dismissing the fourth member means removing the fourth letter of the quintet's name

parts.note: Schubert's famous quintet is known as the Trout

explanation.surface: A musician is hurried off when a quintet drops its fourth player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss fourth member of' removes U, the fourth letter of TROUT, Schubert's Trout Quintet.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's gait between walking and cantering, or a person's jog, is a brisk pace.

clue.text: Putting bill into folder is easily done

indicators.note: into says the bill goes inside the folder

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Filing an invoice away is no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' is a link; 'into' places the bill inside the folder. A bill as AC (account) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achieved without effort, or superficially simple, is effortless and glib.

clue.text: Peer and monarch about to fall for very easy clue?

indicators.note: the peer and the monarch together wrap round the falling word

parts.note: a nob is slang for an aristocrat or toff
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard crossword monarch
to rain is to fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A lord and a queen are about to tumble from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the peer and monarch, side by side, enclose the falling word. 'to fall' reads as part of 'about to', but it is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Something needing no thought at all is a simple matter, and a clue like that is trivially solved.

clue.text: Enthusiasm is to blow over

parts.note: wind that blows in a burst is a gust
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone's keenness is about to fizzle out.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with relish or zest is doing it with great energy and eagerness.

clue.text: No one being honest, except one Liberal, in Coalition

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so one letter is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: if no one is honest then everybody is telling untruths, all lying
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that every coalition politician lies, save one Liberal Democrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except' takes one of the three Ls out of ALL LYING. The surface nods to the UK's Conservative–Liberal Democrat coalition government.
explanation.definitionFit: Joining forces with another party is forming an alliance, i.e. being in coalition with it.

clue.text: Hard part of course: artful to comprehend that

indicators.note: to comprehend is literally to take in or include, so one word holds another

parts.note: artful means cunning, sly
a tee is part of a golf course, where each hole starts

explanation.surface: A tough section of a golf course that a crafty player must understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to comprehend' means include, not understand. 'Hard' looks like a description of the course section, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with the hardness of metal is described as firm and unyielding, like steel.

clue.text: Bank robber's lead shot does for horse

parts.note: Clyde Barrow, of Bonnie and Clyde, was a famous American bank robber

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bank robber's bullet kills a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead shot' looks like bullets but splits into fodder and the anagram indicator 'shot'. Clydesdale is also a Scottish bank.
explanation.definitionFit: This heavy Scottish draught breed is a type of large working horse.

clue.text: Two kids lost? New angle: three lads lost

indicators.note: lost here means scattered and astray, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A worried note about two children gone missing, then three boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' (the second one) mixes up N, ANGLE, THREE and LADS. The definition is the fairy tale of two children abandoned in the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm brothers' story tells of a brother and sister left astray in a forest.

clue.text: Huge train crash is not so good

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A massive railway accident is described as bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' rearranges HUGETRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being more badly behaved, as a child might be, means worse behaved, the comparative of mischievous.

clue.text: Part of bird cooked for beater

definitions.meaning: the lower leg of a roast chicken or turkey
the stick used to strike a drum

explanation.surface: A piece of roast fowl used to bang on something.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a cooked fowl's lower leg and the stick a percussionist plays with.

clue.text: Fully grown, about to take responsibility for such poor posture

definitions.note: the clue names the posture; the answer is the adjective describing someone with it

indicators.note: the word for fully developed wraps around the word for bearing a burden

parts.note: rounded can mean fully developed
to shoulder a task is to take responsibility for it

explanation.surface: A grown-up taking on burdens ends up stooping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has the word for fully developed go round the burden-bearing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose upper back curves forward, with stooped shoulders, has a slouching stance.

clue.text: Crop in drought-ridden conditions — that could be curtains

indicators.note: in says the crop sits inside the dry conditions

parts.note: drought means conditions are dry
rape, or oilseed rape, is a farm crop

explanation.surface: A crop in a drought may be doomed, curtains for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' looks like the slang for the end, fitting the drought, but is literal fabric hangings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging fabric at windows, such as curtains, is a typical example of cloth arranged in folds.

clue.text: Fabric of college plastered with amateur work

indicators.note: plastered with means covered by, so the college sits inside the amateur work

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is amateur home improvement
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A college building badly plastered by home-improvement enthusiasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered with' means covered, so the American college sits inside the do-it-yourself abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A light cotton cloth with raised stripes is a woven textile.

clue.text: Try boarding ship, a cutter

indicators.note: boarding a ship means getting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a judge hears a case when trying it

explanation.surface: An attempt to board a vessel that is itself a cutter, a small sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is what a judge does to a case. 'cutter' suggests a boat, fitting the ship surface, but it means a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Large two-bladed scissors used for clipping hedges or fleeces are a cutting tool.

clue.text: Foreign food makes us hiccup — a bit

indicators.note: a bit means only a part of the phrase is used, the letters sitting within it

explanation.surface: Eating a dish from abroad gives someone a touch of hiccups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit' looks like 'slightly' but signals the letters within maKES US HIccup.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish is a cuisine from abroad.

clue.text: Order to attend final battle

parts.note: a sum is the final total reached by adding up
Mons, in Belgium, was the site of a famous First World War battle in 1914

explanation.surface: A command to report for the last fight of a war.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal writ or call requiring someone to appear, as in court, is an order to be present.

clue.text: Well, chicken's lost its head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped from the bird

parts.note: a boiler is a chicken suitable for boiling

explanation.surface: A chicken has been beheaded, and that is that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost its head' removes B from BOILER. 'Well' looks like a sentence opener but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America a productive oil well is also known by this name.

clue.text: Try to win female, as dog may be going

parts.note: to woo is to try to win someone's affection

explanation.surface: A dog courting a female, as dogs do.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise a canine makes when it barks is rendered in English as this sound.

clue.text: Offer view of old wood

parts.note: pine is a kind of wood

explanation.surface: Someone gives an opinion about some antique timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To express an opinion or give one's thoughts is to put forward a view.

clue.text: Trace call: isn't one criminal?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Police tracing a phone call ask whether the caller is a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges CALL, ISNT and I. 'Trace' looks like a verb about tracing a call but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny spark or particle of something is a minute amount, a mere hint.

clue.text: Many subtle hints that are not consciously taken

parts.note: forty stands for an indefinitely large number
a wink is a sly signal or hint

explanation.surface: Lots of quiet signals go unnoticed by whoever they are aimed at.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'taken': one takes a nap, and does so while dozing, not consciously.
explanation.definitionFit: A short daytime nap is taken while asleep, hence without awareness.

clue.text: Scottish bank courageous? Not very

indicators.note: not having the word very means its abbreviation is removed

parts.note: courageous means brave

explanation.surface: Asking whether a Scottish bank is brave, and deciding not very.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes V (very) from BRAVE. 'bank' is a hillside, not a lender.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect a hillside or steep slope beside a river is called by this word.
